Consider the functions $y: R^{3} → R^{2}$ and $f: R^{2} → R^{2}$, defined by
$y(x) = \begin{bmatrix}x_{1}x_{2}x_{3} \\ x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3}\end{bmatrix}, f(y) = \begin{bmatrix}y_{1} + y_{2} \\ y_{1}y_{2}\end{bmatrix}$.
What is
$\frac{d}{dx}f(y(x))$ evaluated at
$x_{0} = \begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}$?

| $\left.\frac{d}{dx}f(y(x))\right\|_{x_{0}} =$ |  | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} | {{field-3}} |  |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
|  | $42$ | {{field-4}} | $18$ |  |  |

Consider the functions $y: R^{2} → R^{2}$ and $f: R^{2} → R^{2}$, defined by
$y(x) = \begin{bmatrix}\frac{1}{2}(x_{1}^{2} + x_{2}^{2}) \\ x_{1} + x_{2}\end{bmatrix}, f(y) = \begin{bmatrix}y_{1}y_{2} \\ y_{1}^{2} + y_{2}^{2}\end{bmatrix}$.
What is
$\frac{d}{dx}f(y(x))$ evaluated at
$x_{0} = \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}$?

| $\left.\frac{d}{dx}f(y(x))\right\|_{x_{0}} =$ |  | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} |  |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
|  | $4$ | {{field-3}} |  |  |
